capabilities.name: Publish/Subscribe Messaging
capabilities.notes: Core function of NSQ. Supports pub/sub with topics and channels, ensuring message delivery to subscribers. Decentralized architecture ensures no single point of failure.

capabilities.name: Message Persistence
capabilities.notes: NSQ persists messages to disk (via backend queue interface) to ensure reliability across restarts. Dockerfile exposes /data volume for persistence.

capabilities.name: Service Discovery & Routing
capabilities.notes: nsqlookupd component provides service discovery and routing information to nsqd instances and clients.

capabilities.name: Priority Queuing
capabilities.notes: Internal implementation of priority queues for in-flight messages, allowing prioritization of message delivery.

capabilities.name: Web Administration UI
capabilities.notes: nsqadmin provides a web-based interface for monitoring and managing NSQ clusters.

constraints: Persistent storage volume required for message durability (/data)
No external runtime dependencies (statically linked binary)

assumptions: Assumes ability to deploy nsqd and nsqlookupd in a cluster
Assumes client libraries can be used for MQTT/HTTPS ingestion (may require wrapper)
Assumes WebSocket support is available via HTTP API or custom implementation

evidence.claim: NSQ is a realtime distributed messaging platform
Supports distributed and decentralized topologies with fault tolerance
Backend queue interface for persistent storage
Priority queue implementation for in-flight messages

description: NSQ is a realtime distributed messaging platform designed for high throughput and low latency. It provides a decentralized topology for publish/subscribe messaging with reliable delivery guarantees. The system consists of nsqd (daemon), nsqlookupd (discovery/routing), and nsqadmin (web UI). It supports multiple client libraries and binary protocols over TCP.
deployment_constraints: Persistent storage volume required for message durability (/data)
No external runtime dependencies (statically linked binary)
known_gaps: No native MQTT protocol support (requires proxy or wrapper)
No native WebSocket support for real-time updates (requires custom implementation or proxy)
No built-in emergency alert priority handling beyond message priority queues
risks: MIT License is permissive but lacks patent protection
Go 1.25.0 requirement may be future-dated or typo (current stable is ~1.21)
No native MQTT/WebSocket support requires additional infrastructure for requested interfaces
